transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess mostly I’m here because I’ve just been really tired. Not like normal tired, exactly—sleep doesn’t seem to fix it. I can still do things, but even small stuff like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class feels like a lot sometimes. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been bothering me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. Maybe a little low sometimes, but it feels more like being worn out than sad, if that makes sense. I don’t want to overstate it.
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Yeah… maybe a little. I mean, I still want to be the kind of person who does those things, but I haven’t really been caring about them the same way. Like sketching, going to gallery openings, cooking, yoga… even tennis with a friend. Those usually make me feel like myself, and lately I just kind of… don’t reach for them. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or sad most days lately?
Um… I don’t think it’s most days, no. I have moments where I feel kind of low or flat, but I wouldn’t want to say I’m sad all the time. It’s more like… I’m not as bright, maybe? Does that make sense?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

I’m not totally sure… I mean, my sleep hasn’t felt perfect, but I don’t know if I’d call it “trouble sleeping.” Some nights are just kind of off, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you have difficulty falling asleep?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really been tracking. I mean, sometimes I lie there a bit and my mind’s not totally quiet, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe normal? I’m not sure what counts as difficulty.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or worried lately?

I don’t think unusually anxious, no… I mean, I worry about normal things, but I wouldn’t say it’s been out of control or anything. At least, I don’t think so. Is that okay—like, is that what you mean by unusually worried?
Did this tiredness start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

I guess… yes, kind of. It’s been going on for maybe about four months, around when things with my spouse started getting more tense—more arguments than before. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s probably when I noticed the pattern starting.
Has this been interfering with your work or daily responsibilities?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m managing, but not as well as I’d like. I’ve fallen behind on my certificate coursework, and things like bills, meals, and house stuff kind of pile up because I make plans and then don’t really follow through consistently.

My spouse has had to step in more at home, which I feel bad about. And I’ve pulled back some from friends and art things I usually care about. I don’t know if that counts as “interfering,” but it’s definitely been harder.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?
Not really… I mean, I feel bad when I don’t keep up with things the way I should, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless. Maybe guilty sometimes in a normal way? I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… a bit. It’s not like I can’t think at all, but I get kind of stuck. Like I’ll have my planning app open and I’ll just sit there trying to decide whether I should do a class assignment, pay a bill, or start dinner, and somehow I don’t choose any of them for a while. It sounds silly when I say it, but that’s been happening.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?

Um… I don’t think so. I’ve had off days, definitely, but “down or depressed nearly every day” feels stronger than what I’d say. I’m not trying to minimize it—I just don’t think that’s been the main thing. Does that make sense?
During this past month, was there any period of at least two weeks when you felt down, sad, or empty most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think there was a full two-week stretch like that, no. I mean, I’ve had some sad or kind of empty moments, but not most of the day nearly every day. At least… not that I noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you wake up in the night, do you have trouble falling back asleep?
I’m not totally sure. I do wake up sometimes, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether it takes me a long time to fall back asleep. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

I don’t think I’d call it hopeless, exactly. I’ve had moments where I feel unsure or kind of discouraged, but not like… no future or anything. At least I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
On nights when your sleep feels off, do you wake up earlier than you want to and can’t get back to sleep?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I might wake up earlier sometimes, but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I can’t get back to sleep. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. Does that make sense?
Over the past month, have you felt low or down most days?

I don’t think it’s been most days, no. I mean, I’ve had some off days where I feel kind of low or not myself, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe it comes and goes? Is that an okay way to answer?
During the past month, was there a period of at least two weeks when you had much less interest or pleasure in things nearly every day?

I guess… yes, there was a stretch like that. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I kind of stopped caring about the things that normally make me feel like myself—sketching, going to gallery openings, cooking, yoga… even tennis with a friend. It wasn’t like I hated them, I just didn’t really feel pulled toward them. Does that count as what you mean?
During that stretch when you lost interest in things, did your appetite change noticeably?

A little, yeah. I mean, I don’t think it was anything extreme, but my appetite was definitely off. Some days I’d kind of realize I’d only had coffee and maybe a few bites of something all day. And my jeans have been looser, even though I wasn’t trying to lose weight. Does that seem like the kind of change you mean?
During that stretch, did you feel like you were moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

Yeah… I think so, at least on some days. I don’t know if it would’ve been obvious to everyone, but it felt like my body was moving through wet cement. Even answering my spouse if they asked me something simple could take me this weirdly long time, like I had to push the words out. Does that count?
